fixes.explanation: Good guess, because Jesus taught the people beside the sea earlier in this passage. But to Levi, the man at the tax booth, He says something different: “Follow Me.” It's a call to come along with Him, not just to listen. The text says Levi got up and followed Him.

The text never shows Levi asking for any time. Jesus tells him, “Follow Me,” and Levi got up and followed Him. No request for time is mentioned anywhere. I'd probably have asked for a minute to check my oven timer.

The text doesn't name shepherds or farmers at this dinner. It says many tax collectors and sinners were eating with Jesus and His disciples. It also says there were many who followed Him. So the people at Levi's table are the ones the text names.

Nice crafty crowd, but potters and weavers aren't in this passage. The text says many tax collectors and sinners were eating with Jesus and His disciples at Levi's house. It also says there were many who followed Him.
Yes, the scribes who were Pharisees. They see Jesus eating with tax collectors and sinners, and they have a question about it. Notice what the text says about who they ask.
Priests aren't named here. The text says it's the scribes who were Pharisees who see Jesus eating with tax collectors and sinners. They're the ones with the question about this dinner.
Elders aren't mentioned in this scene. The text says the scribes who were Pharisees saw Jesus eating with these people. They're the ones who ask the question about the meal.

That's it, friend. Jesus says, “I have not come to call the righteous, but sinners.” He says it right after, “It is not the healthy who need a doctor, but the sick.” And it's His answer to the scribes who were Pharisees, who had asked His disciples why He eats with tax collectors and sinners.

That's what Jesus says. “But the time will come when the bridegroom will be taken from them…” The picture changes here. First He says, “As long as He is with them, they cannot fast,” and then He looks ahead to a time still coming.

It sounds like a happy ending, but Jesus says something else. The new piece “…will pull away from the old, and a worse tear will result.” The patch is unshrunk cloth, and it's the new piece that pulls away.
